findings.claim: Planned item sql-jdbc-final-mcq-21, as written at the reviewed bytes (map lines 273-283), restated the substance of an existing query-plans-with-explain practice item and a worked page example, so it was a recall repeat, not a step up. That contradicted the record's claim that every item is a step up from topic practice (course-review-and-final-mcq.md line 71) and the blueprint instruction that the questions are harder than the practice quizzes.
findings.recommendation: Re-plan item 21 as a new cross-topic task that topic practice does not set, for example one that joins plan reading (query-plans#o1) with an objective no item elicits yet (indexes#o2). Then update differsFrom and stepUp in value-free terms and rebind the private item.

findings.claim: Planned item sql-jdbc-final-mcq-26, as written at the reviewed bytes (map lines 336-347), was only a small step up from what the transactions-and-acid page and its practice quiz already set. Its one new element was the same rule the topic practice already states, and it had no cross-topic element.
findings.recommendation: Strengthen item 26 with a cross-topic element the topic practice lacks, for example a deciding step drawn from another module's objectives (relational-design key rules, prepared-statements#o3 or transactions#o3). Restate stepUp to match, value-free.

findings.claim: Some stepUp lines at the reviewed bytes said more than an abstract context needs, contradicting the map's own valueFree statement. Line 346 (item 26) named the item's deciding fact; line 245 (item 18) indicated whether a kind of option is keyed. Lines 81 (item 05) and 120 (item 08) named the item's deciding rule rather than its added difficulty.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite those stepUp lines to describe only the added difficulty, without naming any deciding fact, trap, cause, repair or the status of any option. Check every plannedContext, differsFrom and stepUp against the rule that a reader without the private bank cannot infer a key.

findings.claim: Open item 2 understates the Course Review retrieval gap. It names only two JDBC topics (the repository swap point and the test database), but the two Course Review pages retrieve far less of the course. sql-review-joins-grouping-window-functions retrieves joins, WHERE/GROUP BY/HAVING, COUNT and window functions. jdbc-review retrieves the core JDBC query steps, prepared statements, transactions and close order. No Course Review activity retrieves installing-postgres, tables-keys-and-relationships, designing-tables-from-a-user-story, normalization-basics, create-table-data-types-and-constraints, insert-update-and-delete, seeding-sample-data, filtering-and-sorting, handling-nulls (beyond LEFT JOIN NULLs), anti-joins-and-self-joins, subqueries-and-ctes, indexes, query-plans-with-explain or testing-a-repository. That is about 14 of the 22 topics the all-topic final assesses. The module.json description is accurate, but the record and the coverage note in sql-jdbc-course-review/module.json present the gap as two JDBC topics, so the captain does not see the full boundary when deciding.
findings.recommendation: In the record, add a per-topic table of Course Review retrieval (retrieved / not retrieved) for all 22 teaching topics, and restate open item 2 as the full boundary: relational design, CRUD/seeding, filtering, NULLs, anti-joins, subqueries/CTEs, indexes, EXPLAIN and the two JDBC topics have no Course Review retrieval before the final. Leave the remedy to the captain (for example a scenario activity inside the 9-minute SQL review page, which is 6 minutes under the 15-minute cap, or the F24 cumulative-quiz block). Mirror the corrected boundary in the module.json coverage note.

findings.claim: The learner-facing instructions place the 90-minute final on 'Day F24' and call it a 'final check'. The record (course-review-and-final-mcq.md lines 91 and 97) says F24 has a 45-minute Module check block, the day is at least 39 minutes over, and placement is unresolved and held by the captain. If the captain moves the MCQ part off F24 or to another block, the instruction text becomes wrong. Separately, the blueprint id and kind ('sql-module-check', 'moduleCheck') and module.json ('the SQL module check') still say module check, while the instructions and jdbc-review ('Next: the SQL & JDBC course final check') say course final. Learners may meet both names.
findings.recommendation: Until placement is decided, keep the day reference out of the learner instruction sentence (dayId can stay as metadata), or add placement re-verification of the instructions to open item 3. Use one learner-facing name, for example 'SQL & JDBC Foundations final check (SQL module check)', in the instructions, module.json and the review page's next-step line.

findings.claim: The deciding element is unevenly spread. One concept family decides or co-decides 8 of the 30 planned items, and two items share the same trap that topic practice already drills. Meanwhile 4 taught objectives are not elicited by any item: group-by-and-having#o3, indexes#o2, create-table-data-types-and-constraints#o1 and seeding-sample-data#o2. The record lists the 4, and topic-level coverage is complete, so this is a balance issue, not a coverage defect.
findings.recommendation: Without changing the count, move one or two secondary elicitations from the over-represented concept family onto the unelicited objectives (for example indexes#o2 in the re-planned item 21, group-by#o3 in a grouped trace, create-table#o1 in a constraint item). Update objectiveCoverage and the blueprint objective list to match.

findings.claim: Item sql-jdbc-final-mcq-20 is labelled level 'Analyze' while its plannedContext verb is 'Evaluate' ('Evaluate a developer's added index ...'), and its form is the same 'choose' used by the Evaluate items 03, 04 and 28. The level split recorded in course-review-and-final-mcq.md line 71 (7 Apply, 20 Analyze, 3 Evaluate) therefore depends on a label that disagrees with the planned task.
findings.recommendation: Pick one: relabel item 20 as Evaluate and update the md level counts to 7/19/4, or reword the plannedContext to an analysis task (for example 'Analyze which indexes a table already has ...').
